name: Adrian S. Fisher
summary:
Adrian Sanford Fisher was an American lawyer and federal public servant, who served from the late 1930s through the early 1980s. He was associated with the Department of War and Department of State throughout his professional career. He participated in the U.S. government's decision to carry out Japanese-American internment and the international (1945–46) Nuremberg trial, and in State Department Cold War activities during the Harry S.

Truman administration. He was the State Department Legal Adviser under Secretary of State Dean Acheson. Adrian S. Fisher was a legal figures from Memphis (1914-01-21, Memphis–1983-03-18). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Adrian S. Fisher's involvement in the Japanese-American internment and his role as State Department Legal Adviser during the Harry S. Truman administration had significant regional impact on U.S.-Japan relations, while his participation in the Nuremberg trial contributed to the development of international human rights law.
